rv.q: The liveliness ensures the show is never depressing.
The production longs for a little more of the wildly ambitious, teen-fuelled nihilism

Although the production as a whole can feel non-committal, it is an undeniably truthful piece, which effectively captures the fear, frustration and fizzing potential of the most confusing time of life.
But as drama it simply isn’t good enough.
Chandran’s Girl is immediately likeable and recognisable, and her performance carries off this 80-minute entertaining, if often difficult, watch.
It’s utterly familiar and entirely effective.
Not always an easy watch, there’s some superb storytelling in this intriguing portrait of teenage living.
Anyone who has ever been a teenage girl and felt ignored will find plenty to empathise with here.
This iteration may not have the same verve as when Day was in the role, but allows more audience in and does the job smoothly.
In this tour-de-force performance from Charithra Chandran we delve deep into the societal pressures that so many young people face, particularly girls.

cn.t: Critics find Day's teen mental health drama well-intentioned and moving, with praise for Chandran's debut, but opinions split on execution—some laud its honest emotion while others fault predictable plotting and lack of bite.
